How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as
noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record.
Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read. Your comments must be received by 5:00
P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
  Public Comment.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 5, 2024  1
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, March 5, 2024

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Mayor Harrington
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Harrington, Vice Mayor Wu, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Menchaca

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. WOMEN’S HISTORY MONTH

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of February 20, 2024.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of February 20, 2024.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 5, 2024  2
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. RESOLUTION  NO.  24-08  APPROVING  THE  COMPREHENSIVE
  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH THE SAN GABRIEL POLICE
  OFFICERS’ ASSOCIATION FOR THE JULY 1, 2022, THROUGH JUNE 30, 2025
  PERIOD

  On October 4, 2022, the City Council ratified a three-year labor agreement with
  the San Gabriel Police Officers’ Association (POA), covering the July 1, 2022
  through June 30, 2025, period. As part of that agreement, representatives of
  the City and POA agreed to work together to develop a comprehensive
  Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) and incorporate the new labor
  agreement and all previous labor agreements into the comprehensive MOU. In
  December 2023, the parties completed the comprehensive MOU. The
  compensation and benefits outlined in the comprehensive MOU have prior
  approval of the City Council, and as such, approving the comprehensive MOU
  is an administrative function only and will have no fiscal impact.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-08, approving
  the comprehensive Memorandum of Understanding for the period covering
  July 1, 2022, through June 30, 2025, between the City and San Gabriel Police
  Officers’ Association, and authorize the City’s negotiators to fully execute the
  Memorandum of Understanding.

  D. ORDINANCE NO. 702: AMENDING CHAPTER 153 OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO UPDATE THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE
  RELATING TO NEW STATE LAW THAT WOULD ALLOW MEDICINAL
  CANNABIS DELIVERY-ONLY RETAILERS IN THE M-1 ZONE (ZTA23-004) –
  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION

  Ordinance No. 702 was approved at introduction by a 5-0 vote of the City
  Council at the February 20, 2024, City Council meeting. Adoption of Ordinance
  No. 702 would amend Title XV, Chapter 153 (Zoning Code) of the San Gabriel
  Municipal Code relating to new state law that would allow medicinal cannabis
  delivery-only retailers in the M-1 (Light-Manufacturing) Zone (ZTA23-004). The

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 5, 2024  3
   Fiscal Year 2023-24 Adopted Budget includes the cost for required legal
  publication (Account No. 121-702-00-65-000) and codification (Account No.
  121-702-00-22-000) of the ordinance.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: CEQA Guidelines
  Section 15061(b)(3) provides that a project is exempt from CEQA if the activity is
  covered by the commonsense exemption that CEQA only applies to projects which
  have the potential for causing a significant effect on the environment. The
  proposed ordinance qualifies for this CEQA exemption as there is no possibility
  that the ordinance will have a significant effect on the environment as it amends
  the City’s Municipal Code to impose operating requirements on deliver-only
  medicinal cannabis retailers, which does not affect the environment. Accordingly,
  the ordinance is not subject to further environmental review.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  702 entitled “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel,
  California, Approving Planning Case No. ZTA23-004, Amending Title XV,
  Chapter 153 (Zoning) Relating to New State Law that Would Allow Medicinal
  Cannabis Delivery-only Retailers in the M-1 Zone.”

  E. APPROVAL OF FINAL MAP AND SUBDIVISION IMPROVEMENT
  AGREEMENT FOR TRACT NO. 73095, A PROPOSED HOTEL AND MIXED-
  USE DEVELOPMENT LOCATED AT 101 WEST VALLEY BOULEVARD AND
  FINDING OF A CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (CEQA)
  EXEMPTION

  The development located at 101 West Valley Boulevard is a mixed-use
  development building that includes a hotel, retail, restaurant, and residential
  condominium development with two subterranean and six above-ground floor
  levels on a 2.260-acre site. Staff and RKA Consulting Group, Incorporated, the
  City’s contract consultant, have reviewed the Final Tract Map and determined it
  is in compliance with the State Subdivision Map Act, and the City’s Conditions
  of Approval, and the City’s ordinances regarding subdivisions. There is no fiscal
  impact processing an approval of a Final Tract Map.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: A Mitigated
  Negative Declaration has been reviewed and approved by the City’s Planning
  Division for compliance with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  and has filed a Notice of Determination (Public Resources Code, Section 21108
  or 21152). A record of project approval is available to the General Public at the
  Planning Division, City Hall.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 5, 2024  4
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council find the project exempt from California
  Environmental Quality Act based on Section 15332, Class 32 (In-Fill
  Development), approve the Final Tract Map No. 73095 and the Subdivision
  Improvement Agreement, authorize its filing with the Los Angeles County
  Recorder and authorize the City Manager to execute the Subdivision
  Agreement.

  F. MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT WITH THE SAN GABRIEL VALLEY
  COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS FOR THE ACTIVE STREETS MISSION-TO-
  MISSION 2024 EVENT IN THE AMOUNT OF $15,000 PLUS A MAXIMUM
  REIMBURSEMENT OF $10,000

  On January 25, 2024, the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation
  Authority (LACMTA) Board approved the Open Streets Grant Program Cycle
  Five; providing funds for one-day events that close streets to automotive traffic
  and open them to people to walk or bike. On Sunday, April 28, 2024, from 8:40
  a.m. to 3:00 p.m., the cities of San Gabriel, Alhambra and South Pasadena will
  be jointly hosting an open streets event, called Active Streets Mission-to
  Mission. The Transportation Development Act local return funds will be utilized
  to cover the in-kind match requirement of $15,000 and any additional costs
  that exceed the reimbursable amount of $10,000.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This item is not a
  project as defined in Section 15378 of the state CEQA Guidelines, as to its short
  duration, it has no potential for resulting in either a direct physical change in the
  environment, or a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the
  environment.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  the final version of the Memorandum of Agreement between the San Gabriel
  Valley Council of Governments and the cities of San Gabriel, Alhambra, and
  South Pasadena for the 2024 Active Streets Mission-to-Mission, after all three
  agencies mutually agree to the terms.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. EXTENSION OF INTERIM ORDINANCE NO. 701 REGARDING THE
  TEMPORARY MORATORIUM PROHIBITING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 5, 2024  5
   MEDICINAL CANNABIS DELIVERY BUSINESSES AND AN EXEMPTION
  FROM THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT

  The California Legislature adopted Senate Bill 1186 (SB 1186) in 2022, entitled
  the Medicinal Cannabis Patient’s Right of Access Act, which precludes cities and
  counties from adopting or enforcing regulations that prohibit or have the effect
  of prohibiting the retail sale of medicinal cannabis by delivery. SB 1186 took
  effect on January 1, 2024. In order to provide the City with time to adopt
  reasonable regulations for such uses, the City Council on January 16, 2024,
  adopted Interim Urgency Ordinance No. 701 establishing a 45-day temporary
  moratorium. Government Code Section 65658 allows the City Council to further
  extend the Interim Urgency Ordinance by an additional 10 months and 15 days,
  if necessary. A three-month extension of the temporary moratorium is
  necessary to adopt regulations for such uses. There is no fiscal impact
  anticipated from the proposed urgency ordinance.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Environmental
  review is not required under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  pursuant to the California Code of Regulations, Title 14, Chapter 3, Sections
  15060(c)(2) (the activity will not result in a direct or reasonably foreseeable
  indirect physical change in the environment) and 15060(c)(3) (the activity is not
  a project as defined in section 15378) of the CEQA Guidelines, California Code of
  Regulations, Title 14, Chapter 3, because it has no potential to result in a physical
  change to the environment, directly or indirectly. This is because the moratorium
  adopted by the proposed interim ordinance merely prohibits uses that have
  significant impacts on public health, safety, and welfare and does not permit any
  development that could result in a significant change to the environment.
  Furthermore, the moratorium established by the proposed ordinance is
  temporary pending further study and investigation. In addition, the proposed
  ordinance is categorically exempt from CEQA pursuant to Section 15308 of the
  CEQA guidelines because this ordinance is a regulatory action taken by the City
  in accordance with Government Code Section 65858 to assure maintenance and
  protection of the environment pending further review of the potential impacts of
  medical marijuana facilities and mobile medical marijuana dispensaries in the
  City and potential modifications to the San Gabriel Municipal Code.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council extend Interim Ordinance No. 701 for
  three additional months by at least a four-fifths vote of the City Council.

  Alternative Option for Consideration

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 5, 2024  6
   Do not extend the Interim Ordinance. This will leave the City vulnerable to
  dispensary operators entering the City without any established regulations or
  restrictions on location.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. PUBLIC OPINION POLL RESULTS ON PUBLIC SAFETY HEADQUARTER
  PROPERTY TAX AND BUSINESS TAX MODERNIZATION

  A public opinion polling firm, Fairbank, Maslin, Maullin, Metz & Associates (FM3
  Research) was contracted to conduct a public opinion poll to assess the viability
  of an ad valorem property tax for a new public safety headquarters as well as
  changes to the business license tax ordinance that will modernize the code and
  increase the tax. A representative from FM3 Research will present the results of
  the public opinion poll. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the report.

  B. ORDINANCE NO. 703 RENEWING AND APPROVING THE SAN GABRIEL
  POLICE DEPARTMENT’S UPDATED MILITARY EQUIPMENT USE POLICY 707
  AND FINDING THAT THE ANNUAL MILITARY EQUIPMENT REPORT IS IN
  COMPLIANCE WITH GOVERNMENT CODE 7072(A)

  On August 16, 2022, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. 684 approving a
  Military Equipment Use Policy (“Policy”) pursuant to Assembly Bill 481 (“AB 481”).
  In accordance with the legislation and the Policy, a military equipment report
  must be submitted to the City Council annually for each type of military
  equipment approved within one year of approval, and annually thereafter for as
  long as the military equipment is available for use. Adoption of this Ordinance
  would renew and update Lexipol policy 707, approve the annual Military
  Equipment List as required by Government Code Section 7072(a) and establish
  a new adoption process for any further changes to the Military Equipment List.
  No funding has been used to acquire any new military equipment defined by
  Government Code Section 7070 during this reporting period.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 5, 2024  7
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and approve the Assembly Bill
  481 annual report and the updated Policy 707 and by majority vote renew,
  introduce and conduct the first reading by title only of Ordinance No. 703
  Readopting Police Department Lexipol Policy, Section 707, Military
  Equipment, Pursuant to Assembly Bill 481 Military Equipment Acquisition,
  Use, and Reporting and Establishing Annual Review Process, waive future
  reading, and schedule the second reading and adoption for the next regular City
  Council meeting.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The City Council will adjourn the meeting in honor and memory of Cang Lieu, a
  100-year resident of San Gabriel. Cang dedicated and served the community for
  decades by volunteering and contributing to numerous community service events.

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, March 19, 2024 at
  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be
  available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF MARCH 5, 2024
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Harrington called the regu lar meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
  6:30 P.M. on Tuesday, March 5, 2024, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South
  Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Harrington.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, Denise Menchaca, Vice Mayor
  John Wu, and Mayor John R. Harrington.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux, Community Services Director Rebecca Perez,

I  Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City
  Engineer Greg de Vinck, Human Resources/Risk
  Management Director Edward Macias, Fire Chief Steven
  Wallace, Community Development Director Aldo
  Cervantes, Police Chief Edward Elizalde, and Assistant
  City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  how to request meeting agendas.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Harrington announced that the agenda order was
  approved.
  2. PRESENTATIONS

I
  A. WOMEN'S HISTORY MONTH

  Mayor Harrington made the presentation and the following business owners
  accepted the proclamation: Yonette Alleyne, Caribbean Gourmet; Roxane Guzman,
  Lunas Restaurant; and Carina Rivera, El Pavo Bakery.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Carina Rivera, resident, provided comments expressing concerns with the Human
  Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR) Commission involving youth in the discussion of
  sensitive topics.

  CITY COUNCIL REGU LAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 5  March 5, 2024
   A resident of 25 years provided comments about a voter's guide she received from a
  Council Member.

  Jayson Hugh, new Field Representative for Assemblymember Mike Fong, introduced
  himself and stated he is looking forward to working with the City.

  Cheryl Cabot, resident and Community Services Commissioner, expressed displeasure
  at comments made at a recent HEAR Commission meeting, and reminded the

I  Commission of their role.

  Andrew, resident, stated his support for the All Are Welcome program, as proposed
  by the HEAR Commission.

  Chasity Jennings-Nunez, M.D., resident, and HEAR Commission Chair, thanked the
  business owners recognized for Women's History Month for their contributions to the
  community, and spoke in support of the All Are Welcome program as proposed by
  the HEAR Commission.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Regarding Item 4B, Andrew, resident, questioned if the City receives restitution to the
  City for graffiti, and requested details on a payment to the San Gabriel Hope Lions
  Club.

  City Manager Lazzaretto responded that the City does receive restitution for graffiti
  very infrequently and it doesn't come close to the actual cost to the City, and that the
  payments are for Council Member memberships or participation in events.

I  Regarding Item 4F, in response to a question from Council Member Chan, Public
  Works Director/City Engineer de Vinck gave details of the City funds and in-kind
  donation required for the event and where funding will come from.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Vice Mayor Wu, to
  approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4F as presented.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved:

I  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of February 20, 2024.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of February 20, 2024.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved February 9, and February 16, 2024, Registers of
  Demands and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 5  March 5, 2024
   C. RESOLUTION NO. 24-08 APPROVING THE COMPREHENSIVE MEMORANDUM
  OF UNDERSTANDING WITH THE SAN GABRIEL POLICE OFFICERS'
  ASSOCIATION FOR THE JULY 1, 2022 THROUGH JUNE 30, 2025 PERIOD

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 24-08, approving the comprehensive
  Memorandum of Understanding for the period covering July 1, 2022 through June
  30, 2025 between the City and San Gabriel Police Officers' Association, and
  authorized the City's negotiators to fully execute the Memorandum of
  Understanding.

I  D. ORDINANCE NO. 702: AMENDING CHAPTER 153 OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO UPDATE THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE
  RELATING TO NEW STATE LAW THAT WOULD ALLOW MEDICINAL
  CANNABIS DELIVERY-ONLY RETAILERS IN THE M-1 ZONE (ZTA23-004) -
  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION

  The City Council waived reading and adopted Ordinance No. 702 entitled "An
  Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel, California, Approving
  Planning Case No. ZTA23-004, Amending Title XV, Chapter 153 (Zoning) Relating
  to New State Law that Would Allow Medicinal Cannabis Delivery-only Retailers in
  the M-1 Zone."

  E. APPROVAL OF FINAL MAP AND SUBDIVISION IMPROVEMENT AGREEMENT
  FOR TRACT NO. 73095, A PROPOSED HOTEL AND MIXED-USE DEVELOPMENT
  LOCATED AT 101 WEST VALLEY BOULEVARD AND FINDING OF A CALIFORNIA
  ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (CEQA) EXEMPTION

  The City Council found the project exempt from California Environmental Quality

I  Act based on Section 15332, Class 32 (In-Fill Development), approved the Final
  Tract Map No. 73095 and the Subdivision Improvement Agreement, authorized its
  filing with the Los Angeles County Recorder and authorized the City Manager to
  execute the Subdivision Agreement.

  F. MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT WITH THE SAN GABRIEL VALLEY COUNCIL
  OF GOVERNMENTS FOR THE ACTIVE STREETS MISSION-TO-MISSION 2024
  EVENT IN THE AMOUNT OF $15,000 PLUS A MAXIMUM REIMBURSEMENT OF
  $10,000

  The City Council authorized the City Manager to execute the final version of the
  Memorandum of Agreement between the San Gabriel Valley Council of
  Governments and the cities of San Gabriel, Alhambra, and South Pasadena for the
  2024 Active Streets Mission-to-Mission, after all three agencies mutually agree to
  the terms.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING

I  A. EXTENSION OF INTERIM ORDINANCE NO. 701 REGARDING THE TEMPORARY
  MORATORIUM PROHIBITING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF MEDICINAL
  CANNABIS DELIVERY BUSINESSES AND AN EXEMPTION FROM THE
  CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT

  Mayor Harrington opened the public hearing.

  Planning Manager Samantha Tewasart made the staff presentation.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 5  March 5, 2024
   There was no public comment; therefore, Mayor Harrington closed the public
  hearing.

  A motion was made by Council Member Chan, seconded by Council Member
  Menchaca, to extend Interim Ordinance No. 701 for three additional months.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON

I
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS - None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. PUBLIC OPINION POLL RESULTS ON PUBLIC SAFETY HEADQUARTERS
  PROPERTY TAX AND BUSINESS TAX MODERNIZATION

  City Manager Lazzaretto introduced the item and Consultant Richard Bernard of
  FM3 made the presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included survey results on favorable versus unfavorable views
  of City government.

  Andrew, resident, commented on the survey and the need for additional
  information for the community.

I  Discussion included next steps including analysis, educating the community, and
  presenting options to the Council and community; and survey methodology.

  B. ORDINANCE NO. 703 RENEWING AND APPROVING THE SAN GABRIEL
  POLICE DEPARTMENT'S UPDATED MILITARY EQUIPMENT USE POLICY 707
  AND FINDING THAT THE ANNUAL MILITARY EQUIPMENT REPORT IS IN
  COMPLIANCE WITH GOVERNMENT CODE 7072(A)

  Police Lieutenant Rene Lopez made the presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included that the rifles used now are standard issue so are not
  required to be reported; and the potential purchase of unarmed aerial vehicles
  (drones) and associated personnel needs.

  Andrew, resident, expressed his opinion that the report as presented is insufficient
  to conform with current law.

I
  In response to a question from Council, City Attorney Lemieux stated that the
  policy is compliant with the law.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Vice Mayor Wu,
  to approve the Assembly Bill 481 annual report and the updated Policy 707 and
  renew, introduce and conduct the first reading by title only of Ordinance No. 703
  Readopting Police Department Lexipol Policy, Section 707, Military Equipment,
  Pursuant to Assembly Bill 481 Military Equipment Acquisition, Use, and Reporting
  and Establishing Annual Review Process, waive future reading, and schedule the
  second reading and adoption for the next regular City Council meeting.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 5  March 5, 2024
   Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT - None.
